name: KyberSlash
note: Secret-dependent division. On a target with a constant-time divider the same source is constant time, so origin is hardware-implicit: the violation is introduced by instruction selection. Addresses do not vary, which is what makes it invisible to differential address-trace analysis.

name: Minerva
note: Nonce bit-length leaks through scalar multiplication time; a few hundred to a few thousand signatures suffice via lattice reduction. The upstream artifact publishes collected datasets, so this class is recoverable offline.

name: LadderLeak
note: Distinguished from Minerva by observable: the signal is recovered through microarchitectural observation of the ladder's control flow rather than through wall-clock latency, so an address-trace analyser can in principle see it and a latency-only method cannot.

name: TPM-FAIL
note: Black-box timing of a hardware and a firmware TPM. origin is api-level because the implementation is not available to any analyser at any level: nothing that reads source, IR or binary can be pointed at it. This is the class that bounds what a source-or-binary corpus can ever cover.

name: HQC and BIKE rejection sampling
note: Rejection sampling whose running time depends on a seed derived from the secret message.

name: OpenSSL 1.0.1u ECDSA nonce leakage
note: Found by differential address-trace analysis with no taint annotation, which is the standing counterexample to any claim that internally generated secrets are unreachable.

exclusion_reason: not a timing side channel. The first nine bits of the P-521 nonce are zero by construction, so roughly sixty signatures suffice with no observation channel at all. It is a randomness defect exploited by the same lattice machinery as the nonce-leakage class, and admitting it would make the corpus measure something no constant-time analyser claims to detect.
name: PuTTY biased ECDSA nonce generation
note: Recorded rather than deleted: the class was considered, and the reason it is out of scope is itself a boundary of what this corpus measures.
